original.question: Evaluate $\int_{0}^{\infty}(1-x)e^{-x}\,dx$, showing the integration by parts and the limit.
original.answer:
Parts: $u=1-x$, $dv=e^{-x}dx$, so $du=-dx$, $v=-e^{-x}$.
$\int(1-x)e^{-x}dx=-(1-x)e^{-x}-\int e^{-x}dx=-(1-x)e^{-x}+e^{-x}=xe^{-x}+C$.
$\int_{0}^{\infty}(1-x)e^{-x}dx=\lim_{b\to\infty}\left[xe^{-x}\right]_{0}^{b}=\lim_{b\to\infty}be^{-b}-0$.
$be^{-b}=\frac{b}{e^{b}}$ is of type $\infty/\infty$; L'Hopital gives $\lim\frac{1}{e^{b}}=0$.
So the integral converges, and its value is $0$.

original.question: Evaluate $\int_{1}^{4}\frac{dx}{(x-2)^{2/3}}$.
original.answer:
The integrand is infinite at $x=2$, inside $[1,4]$, so split: $\int_{1}^{2}+\int_{2}^{4}$ and test each.
$\int_{1}^{2}(x-2)^{-2/3}dx=\lim_{k\to2^{-}}\left[3(x-2)^{1/3}\right]_{1}^{k}=3\left(0-(-1)\right)=3$.
$\int_{2}^{4}(x-2)^{-2/3}dx=\lim_{k\to2^{+}}\left[3(x-2)^{1/3}\right]_{k}^{4}=3\sqrt[3]{2}-0=3\sqrt[3]{2}$.
Both converge, so the integral converges to $3+3\sqrt[3]{2}$.
